signals.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group ‘The Gentlemen?’
signals.summary: A cybercrime group known as The Gentlemen has emerged as the second most active ransomware gang by victim count, rapidly attracting a talented pool of hackers through an aggressive recruitment strategy that promises affiliates 90 percent of any ransom paid by victims. This post examines clues pointing to a real life identity for the administrator of The Gentlemen ransomware group.

signals.title: A Record-Breaking Patch Tuesday for June 2026
signals.summary: Microsoft today released software updates to plug nearly 200 security holes across its Windows operating systems and supported software, a record number of fixes for the company's monthly Patch Tuesday cycle. Nearly three dozen of those bugs earned Microsoft's most dire "critical" rating, and exploit code for at least three of the weaknesses is now publicly available.

signals.title: How has use of framing protection security headers changed in the past 3 years?, (Wed, Jun 10th)
signals.summary: Back in 2023, I wrote a diary[ 1 ] discussing how commonly X-Frame-Options and CSP headers containing the frame-ancestors directive were used on 1 million most popular domains on the internet (based on the Tranco list[ 2 ]), and how they were set. signals.title: Microsoft June 2026 Patch Tuesday, (Tue, Jun 9th)
signals.summary: Microsoft today released patches for 204 vulnerabilities. 38 of these vulnerabilities are considered critical, and three have been disclosed before today. Six of the vulnerabilities affect Microsoft cloud solutions and do not require any user action. In addition, Microsoft incorporated 360 different vulnerabilities affecting Chromium into its Edge browser.

signals.title: TeamPCP Supply Chain Campaign: Activity Through 2026-06-07, (Mon, Jun 8th)
signals.summary: This diary continues the Internet Storm Center&#;x26;#;39;s tracking of the TeamPCP supply chain campaign, first documented in the SANS white paper When the Security Scanner Became the Weapon and most recently in the handler diary Activity Through 2026-05-24 . Since that update, the story moved into two new places: the United States government, which formally caught up to the campaign, and the wider population of attackers now wielding the Mini Shai-Hulud framework that TeamPCP open-sourced last month.

signals.title: Mini Shai-Hulud: Where SLSA’s Boundaries Fall
signals.summary: The “Mini Shai-Hulud” attack chained a GitHub Actions workflow misconfiguration, cache poisoning, and OIDC token extraction to publish malicious packages through legitimate CI/CD pipelines.
